title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One day of sales lost; 14.3% of week. No prior closures at this store. Sales are typically spread across week, so 1/7 reduction is reasonable.

drivers.name: Price increase (+4.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $13.93: 27 (9% below baseline) and 21 (16% below). No prior price increase at this level. Noise-adjusted estimate shrinks effect; conservative -10% used.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 24.9. No events or promotions are scheduled. The store closure on Monday (2026-11-09) reduces the selling days by 1/7 (~14.3%), likely reducing sales proportionally. The price increase to $13.93 (+4.1%) is above prior levels, and recent weeks at this price (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw 27 and 21 units—10% and 16% below baseline. No past price hikes at this level have been tested, but the downward trend is consistent. The noise-adjusted effect of price increases is uncertain but likely negative. The classical uplift model gives 1.00, but that ignores the price rise and closure. Adjust down for both. The closure is a clear driver; price is a moderate one. Combined multiplicative effect shrinks toward 1.0 due to limited evidence.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 13.93 (+4.1% vs regular price 13.38)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 24.9 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 62.7 | 10%-90%: 2.9 - 43.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
